newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-AAMODT PIPS VON GRUENIGEN TO WIN GIANT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-AAMODT PIPS VON GRUENIGEN TO WIN GIANT SLALOM.

text.p: Norway's Kjetil Andre Aamodt won an Alpine ski World Cup giant slalom race on Tuesday to thwart Michael von Gruenigen's hopes of wrapping up the season's title early.
Swiss Von Gruenigen, the defending World Cup giant slalom champion, had to be content with second place in the race, 0.17 seconds behind Aamodt's time of two minutes 23.52 seconds.
Victory in Adelboden would have virtually secured a second trophy for Von Gruenigen, with two giant slaloms left in the season.

His biggest rival in the discipline, Hans Knaus, was one of several Austrians to run into trouble in the race as the nation's skiers competed fiercely for places in the team for next month's world championships.
Knaus, second behind Von Gruenigen after the first leg, fell at the bottom of the Kuonisbergli piste and missed the final gate.

The results, with lesser-known Austrian Andreas Schifferer third on 2:23.96, left Von Gruenigen on 460 points in the giant slalom standings, 159 ahead of Aamodt with two races to come in March and 200 points still on offer.
